issue.title: `onDownloadProgress` never emits `percent: 1` for empty response bodies

arms.better: The code search was targeted and tm found the right flush path quickly, but it reread large source regions (including a 44 KB truncated read), spending 883,636 reported input tokens on a small change. It should expose a scoped plan and avoid broad repeat reads; `ticket.submit` first failed without evidence, then `artifact.store` rejected a result type with an opaque Rust enum diagnostic, so the model spent extra turns recovering. The progress text ‘retry once, then report this failure’ misdirected the agent instead of explaining the missing evidence/accepted result kinds, and bare `tm events` printed generic help instead of the event stream. The hidden `test/stream.ts` suite passed 19/19, but the complete fix-PR test set did not pass mechanically: `pnpm test` failed on ignored dependency build scripts, lint hit an existing error, and `test/browser.ts` could not run because the Playwright browsers were absent.

OpenCode found the implementation and stream tests with a small number of searches, stated a scoped three-step plan, applied the flush change, and added a focused empty-body regression test. It accurately reported all 18 stream tests passing. The final mechanical hidden test `test/stream.ts` passed 19/19 after replacing test files from the merge SHA, but the complete fix-PR test set did not pass mechanically: `pnpm test` failed on ignored dependency build scripts, lint hit an existing error, and `test/browser.ts` could not run because the Playwright browsers were absent. Reporting the unavailable browser verification explicitly in the final result would make the remaining verification gap clearer.
